subject: Fast matrix group-wise centering: any expert in data.table?

messages.author: f14d4c9d01f43388
messages.subject: Fast matrix group-wise centering: any expert in data.table?
parts:
Hi

I am trying to write a fast function to do matrix group-wise centering: for each variable in the matrix, center the variable by removing the mean, yet the mean is to be calculated at the group level.

dplyr solution is waaay too slow, data.table seems much better, but still could benefit from some improvement ( I am very new to data.table). I wrote some benchmark code and posted on Stack Exchange - Code review, but had little feedback so far: https://codereview.stackexchange.com/questions/203513/group-wise-deviations-from-means-centering-with-dplyr-vs-data-table

If anyone has some good understanding of data.table, or want to throw an alternative (R base ?) solution, that would be greatly appreciated! You could get some virtual points on stack overflow, and a very real coffee on campus :-)

Everything is on the post, but for archiving purpose, here is in a nutshell the question. I found 2 data.table solutions:
- 1) compute for each variable the function x - mean(x), group-wise
- 2) add the mean variables in the data.table, then compute the difference between raw columns and mean columns

Intuitively, 1 should be way faster: we are not adding more variables in the data.table, and doing it in one operation. Yes in practice 2) is faster... why? I might not be using the full benefit of mean optimisation in data.table? How to write it as a anonymous function in the data.table way, instead of the classical way function(x) x - mean(x)

Thanks!!

Matthieu

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Fast matrix group-wise centering: any expert in data.table?
parts:
I've worked with data.table.  I find both the syntax for data.table and dplyr to be fairly convoluted as compared with data.frame, but yes, data.table does things really fast (it cut a data.frame-based workflow runtime from 3 days down to about 10 minutes for me)


Base-R isn't going to be as fast, so you're best off learning data.table as you mentioned..  I'll try to look at your SE thread later. Would you prefer if I post to there or to this list? (I'm mpag on SE)
